papers.what_it_is: A proof-of-concept simulation of a quantum generalized linear model on Xanadu's continuous-variable (qumode) simulator, tested on simulated overdispersed data and the UCI Forest Fires dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that QGLMs provide ~10% gain over the next best algorithm on the UCI Forest Fires dataset.
quotes: In fact, QGLMs provide ~10% gain over the next best algorithm on this dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: One dataset, one simulated run set, the authors' own comparison.
assertions.reader_inference: The result comes from a classical simulation of a photonic circuit, with a t-SNE reduction, one small dataset and no stated significance test.

assertions.value: The authors report that QGLMs yield slightly worse prediction on the simulated overdispersed dataset.
quotes: QGLMs yield slightly worse prediction on the simulated dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated-data result stated by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that t-SNE reduced the predictors to 4 components to be compatible with Xanadu's capabilities, and that algorithms were run on the same training and test set 10 times apiece to average out quantum effects.
quotes: t-SNE was used to reduce the dimensionality of the predictor set to 4 components to make it compatible with Xanadu's capabilities.
algorithms were run on the same training and test set 10 times apiece to average out quantum effects.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

papers.what_it_is: A variational quantum linear solver based quantum power flow method for NISQ devices, tested on five-bus and nine-bus systems.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the five-bus test system the compiled circuit depth of NISQ-QPF is 15, against 14811 for HHL-QPF on the same quantum basis.
quotes: the depth of the compiled circuit optimized from the devised NISQ-QPF algorithm is 15, which is smaller than that of the HHL-QPF method (i.e., 14811) on the same quantum basis.
assertions.certainty_reason: One test system, compiled-depth count from the authors' own run.

assertions.value: The authors state that case studies validate the effectiveness and accuracy of NISQ-QPF on IBM's real, noisy quantum devices.
quotes: Promising case studies validate the effectiveness and accuracy of NISQ-QPF on IBM's real, noisy quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' summary of their own case studies; the tests are small systems.
assertions.reader_inference: Hardware runs cover a nine-bus system only, per Section IV.B.

assertions.value: The authors state that QPF is validated in a five-bus test system and a nine-bus test system, run on an IBM quantum simulator and a practical quantum machine (IBMQ belem).
quotes: This section validates the effectiveness and accuracy of QPF in a typical five-bus test system (see Fig.2) and a nine-bus test system.
QPF is implemented on an IBM quantum simulator (IBMQ qasm simulator) with Qiskit(0.16.0) and a practical quantum machine (IBMQ belem).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own test scope.

papers.title_in_file: Towards interpretable quantum machine learning via single-photon quantum walks
papers.what_it_is: A variational method to quantize projective simulation, a reinforcement learning model, using single-photon quantum walks in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer lattice, shown numerically on a transfer-learning task.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in an example from transfer learning, the quantized PS model can exploit quantum interference to acquire capabilities beyond those of its classical counterpart.
quotes: we show that the quantized PS model can exploit quantum interference to acquire capabilities beyond those of its classical counterpart.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result on one constructed scenario.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is to a classical PS agent in a scenario the authors chose to pronounce the difference.

assertions.value: The authors state that a classical agent can achieve at most an accuracy of 8/9 in the transfer-learning scenario, always lower than the quantum agent's accuracy.
quotes: A classical agent can achieve at most an accuracy AC = 8/9 (horizontal line, for both plots), always lower than AQ.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result on one constructed scenario, from the authors' own simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that one limitation of the Gram-Schmidt update is that it assumes perfect knowledge and control of the experimental settings.
quotes: One limitation is that it assumes perfect knowledge and control of the experimental settings.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit.

papers.title_in_file: Quadratic Advantage with Quantum Randomized Smoothing Applied to Time-Series Analysis
papers.what_it_is: Quantum randomized smoothing (QuAdRo) with Grover's algorithm for robustness certificates, with k-Hamming-distant bit-flip perturbations, simulated on Iris and GunPoint.

assertions.value: The authors state that QuAdRo obtains probabilistic robustness certificates, similar to RS, with a quadratic speed-up in the number of shots required.
quotes: In practice, QuAdRo obtains probabilistic robustness certificates, similar to RS, but with a quadratic speed-up in the number of shots required.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on small tasks; the speed-up is inherited from the QuAdRo method.
assertions.reader_inference: The speed-up is a property of QuAdRo (reference 15) applied here, in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that preparing k-Hamming states instead of uniform states resulted in higher certified accuracy for the same number of shots.
quotes: In our empirical validation, preparing k-Hamming states instead of uniform states resulted in higher certified accuracy for the same number of shots.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated experiment on two small datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the average runtime for the simulated circuit with a 1-Hamming distribution is roughly 21 minutes per sample on a server with a 128 CPU cores and 775 GB of RAM memory.
quotes: The average runtime for the simulated circuit with a 1-Hamming distribution is roughly 21 minutes per sample on a server with a 128 CPU cores and 775 GB of RAM memory.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own simulation timing.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method requires data to be encoded in basis states, does not exactly replicate the distribution of k-Hamming distant states, and requires n additional ancillary qubits.
quotes: it requires data to be encoded in basis states due to the use of the Grover oracle, limiting data encoding options.
Our method, however, does not exactly replicate the distribution of k-Hamming distant states and requires n additional ancillary qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Phases Classification Using Quantum Machine Learning with SHAP-Driven Feature Selection
papers.what_it_is: QSVM and VQC classification of phases of the ANNNI model, with SHAP used to select features, in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that QSVM reached 98.46% accuracy against VQC's 94.81% in the 8-site system, and 97.73% against 96.49% in the 12-site system.
quotes: QSVM outperformed VQC in the cases studied, particularly in the 8-site system, where it achieved an impressive accuracy of 98.46%, compared to VQC's 94.81%.
For the 12-site system, the accuracies for QSVM and VQC were slightly lower at 97.73% and 96.49%, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results on one model family.
assertions.reader_inference: Both models are simulated on a one-dimensional spin model.

assertions.value: The authors report that for both algorithms the optimal performance was achieved when using 5 features.
quotes: For both algorithms, the optimal performance was achieved when using 5 features.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single study result.

assertions.value: The authors state that for systems with 8 and 12 sites they obtain 12 and 18 features, and that the results come from computational simulations.
quotes: Thus, for systems with 8 and 12 sites, we obtain 12 and 18 features, respectively.
Section VI presents the results obtained from the computational simulations
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup and scope.

papers.title_in_file: Should we trade off higher-level mathematics for abstraction to improve student understanding of quantum mechanics?
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (section 1), start of section 2 and Conclusions (section 5); derivation sections skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A physics-education paper that argues for an operator-first, representation-independent course in quantum mechanics with lower mathematics prerequisites.

assertions.value: The authors argue that students can handle the abstraction and that reformulating quantum mechanics so that the required math is high-school math is a viable option.
quotes: We argue in this work that students can handle the abstraction and that option (iii) is a viable one.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author argument; no student outcome data seen in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors state that abstraction is introduced slowly after quantum ideas are established in a conceptual unit that requires about 30% of the total available class time.
quotes: introducing abstraction slowly after we have established quantum ideas in a conceptual unit that requires about 30% of the total available class time.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own course design.

assertions.value: The authors state that students would certainly benefit from studying some linear algebra before moving to follow-on quantum computation and communication classes.
quotes: although they would certainly benefit from studying some linear algebra before doing so
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit on preparation.

papers.title_in_file: Empowering Neural Network-based Quantum Monte Carlo with Local Pseudopotentials
papers.what_it_is: Classical neural-network quantum Monte Carlo for molecular ground states, made cheaper and more accurate with local pseudopotentials (pseudo-Hamiltonians). A classical-ML method for quantum chemistry, not run on a quantum computer.

assertions.value: The authors report that for sulfur-only systems from a single atom to S10, ECP costs were comparable to all-electron, while the pseudo-Hamiltonian achieved more than 10 times acceleration for larger systems.
quotes: We demonstrate the efficiency improvement using a series of sulfur-only systems in Fig. 2a, ranging from a single sulfur atom to S10.
Across all these systems, ECP calculations incur computational cost comparable to AE, while PH is able to achieve more than 10 times acceleration for larger systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own timing runs on sulfur systems.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the sulfur dimer potential energy curve the PH and ECP nonparallelity errors were 2.4 and 2.0 mHa, while the all-electron result showed 12.2 mHa.
quotes: The PH and ECP PECs align closely, both exhibiting low NPEs (respectively 2.4 and 2.0 mHa). AE, however, shows a large NPE (12.2 mHa)
assertions.certainty_reason: One molecule, authors' own calculation.

assertions.value: The authors state that practical applicability depends on the availability of high-quality PHs for specific elements.
quotes: its practical applicability depends on the availability of high-quality PHs for specific elements.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit.

papers.title_in_file: Deep Variational Quantum Eigensolver: a divide-and-conquer method for solving a larger problem with smaller size quantum computers
papers.what_it_is: A divide-and-conquer variational quantum eigensolver that concatenates VQEs through an effective Hamiltonian, demonstrated by simulation on Heisenberg antiferromagnet models.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical results on a 64-qubit system suggest deep VQE provides a good approximation (discrepancy within a few percent), while it is unclear how accurate the ground state energy can be for such a large system.
quotes: While it is unclear how accurate ground state energy can be obtained for such a large system, our numerical results on a 64-qubit system suggest that deep VQE provides a good approximation (discrepancy within a few percent) and has a room for further improvement.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation of proof-of-principle size.
assertions.reader_inference: The 64-qubit case is solved by simulating smaller quantum computers, per the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the proposed scheme enables handling problems of more than 1000 qubits by concatenating VQEs with a few tens of qubits.
quotes: The proposed scheme enables us to handle the problems of > 1000 qubits by concatenating VQEs with a few tens of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' extrapolation; the largest simulated case is smaller.

assertions.value: The authors state that deep VQE applies to large systems with strong intra-subsystem interactions and weak inter-subsystem interactions, and that the demonstrations are proof-of-principle numerical demonstrations on quasi one-dimensional models.
quotes: Deep VQE allows us to apply quantum-classical hybrid algorithms on small-scale quantum computers to large systems with strong intra-subsystem interactions and weak inter-subsystem interactions
As proof-of-principle numerical demonstrations, we use the proposed method for quasi one-dimensional models
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope.
